_comment: Datasheet profile. Curve points were read off the published charts by eye and carry the stated uncertainty; labelled discharge results are exact as printed. Replace or supplement with measured data as it arrives, keeping the datasheet entries for comparison.
name: Tadiran TL-5903 (iXtra)

source.document: Tadiran TL-5903 datasheet, ECN 1501879 Rev. F 04/2020

ratings.nominalCapacityConditions: not stated on the datasheet; no published discharge curve reaches it

dischargeAt25C.note: Labelled results from the 'Discharge characteristics @ +25 C' chart. Plateau voltages are read from the chart to about +/-0.03 V.

capacityVsCurrent.note: From the 'Capacity vs. current' chart, log current axis 0.01-30 mA. At 25 C the labelled discharge results above take precedence where the two disagree (the chart reads about 1.5 Ah at 30 mA against the labelled 1.70 Ah at 31 mA). Low-current capacity falls because self-discharge competes with the load over the years such a discharge takes; it falls further, not less, when warm.

loadedVoltageVsTemperature.note: From the 'Voltage vs. temperature' chart: the voltage the cell holds under a steady load, early in life. Points are [currentMa, volts] at each temperature.

voltageDelay.note: Passivation: the first load after storage sees a voltage dip that recovers as the passivation layer breaks down.

points.pulse: 20 mA for 1 s, no background current, room temperature

openQuestions: Loaded voltage at the 35-75 mA an SD write draws is beyond every published curve; the battery suite measures it on a real cell at each temperature.
End of life is where the loaded voltage, at the sensed temperature and the device's heaviest load, falls to the board's minimum operating voltage (BROWNOUT_HEAVY).
Self-discharge per year is not stated numerically; it is inferred here only through the low-current capacity loss.
